item.title: Preface
item.description:
PREFACE

On November 17, 1962, the publication of the fifth and last Volume of Professor P. V. Kane’s History of Dharmaśāstra was formally announced by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, and a significant landmark in the history of Indological research in this country may be said to have been thereby established. The History of Dharmaśāstra is a literary work which is truly magnificent both in conception and execution. Its five Volumes, which together extend over nearly 6,500 pages, seek to present the most comprehensive treatment of the religious and civil law of ancient and medieval India. And, Professor Kane has accomplished this gigantic task single-handed— incidentally, he has written down every word in the History in his own hand – and that too while he had been occupied with various other literary and public activities. As I have said on another occasion, for Professor Kane, the History of Dharmaśāstra is the crowning glory of a life of great fulfilment, and, for the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, it is a matter of signal pride and honour to have been closely associated with that work.
